definitions.meaning: Materials are issued at the cost of the earliest lot still in stock; when that lot is used up, the next earliest lot is used.
definitions.note: Closing stock carries the latest prices

definitions.meaning: Materials issued are priced at the cost of the latest lot still in stock (received before the issue date); when that lot runs out, the next latest lot is used.
definitions.note: Closing stock carries the oldest prices

doubt.question: Does LIFO issue the lot received last of all?
doubt.answer: No. It uses the latest lot received before the issue date and still in stock. Lots received after the issue date cannot be issued.

exam_tip: Draw a stores ledger with Receipts, Issues and Balance columns. Update the balance lot by lot after every issue.

insight.text: Total cost to account for stays the same; the method only decides how much goes to issues and how much stays in stock.

key_points: Stores ledger records receipts, issues and balance for each material in quantity and value.
==FIFO== issues from the oldest lot in stock first; issue price is the cost of that lot.
==LIFO== issues from the latest lot still in stock; !!lots received after the issue date cannot be used!!.
Under every method, opening stock + receipts = cost issued + closing stock; only the split between issues and closing stock changes.

memory_trick.mnemonic: FIFO = First in the queue, first out
memory_trick.explanation: Picture a ticket queue: the first person leaves first (FIFO). LIFO is a stack of plates: you take the top plate, the latest one placed, still on the stack.}

mistakes.wrong: Under LIFO, using a lot received after the date of issue
mistakes.right: Use only lots received on or before the issue date and still in stock.

mistakes.wrong: Pricing every FIFO issue at the latest purchase price
mistakes.right: FIFO prices issues at the oldest lot in stock; closing stock is at latest prices.

mistakes.wrong: Not moving to the next lot when one lot is exhausted within an issue
mistakes.right: Split the issue: finish the current lot at its price, then take the balance from the next lot at its price.
